exposure: Gestational age at birth (37 weeks, 38 weeks, after 39 weeks)
cohort: The study included 4,669 term infants born at Tokyo Metropolitan Toshima Hospital, categorized by their gestational age at birth.
finding: Early term infants, especially those born at 37 weeks of gestation, demonstrated significantly higher odds of hospitalization, apnea, and hypoglycemia compared to infants born after 39 weeks.
mod_finding: The results suggest that elective cesarean sections would be better planned at 38 weeks of gestational age to avoid the increased risks associated with birth at 37 weeks.
followup_time: N/A (outcomes were short-term, typically within initial hospitalization)
gest_age: 37 weeks and onwards (37, 38, and after 39 weeks of gestation)
